findings.where: First screen, the action row: the 'Write to me' button and the underlined address beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one job is to get the visitor to write to Mark. The button that asks them to write, and the address that looks like a link, both do nothing when clicked. The only working mailto is in the footer, at the very bottom of the page. A visitor who clicks the obvious action and gets nothing has to copy the address by hand or scroll all the way down.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer ready to write to Mark. Their first try at contact fails, which costs the enquiry and reads as a neglected or broken site from a solo advisor.

findings.where: First screen, the action row: 'Book a consultation' next to 'Write to me'
findings.fault: The brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark. The first screen offers two filled buttons of equal weight that compete. The second is a firm's sales line: it suggests a booking service and a paid product the site doesn't have, and its link goes to #consult, a section that isn't on the page.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark. The brief names 'salesy' and a look any consultancy could own as failures, and asks for one action. A procurement reader would also object: they come to judge a person's work, and a 'Book a consultation' button raises the question of fees the page never answers.

findings.where: First screen, the blue margin notes (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024)
findings.fault: The notes name Mark's real talks in link blue, so they look like proof the visitor can open, but none of them goes anywhere. The page's strongest evidence of his work can't be checked from the first screen.
findings.who_objects: A development-agency reader judging Mark against terms of reference. They want to read the talk behind each venue, and a dead blue title reads as a broken promise rather than proof.

findings.where: First screen as a whole (the credibility around the action)
findings.fault: Mark's standing rests on two claims: who he advises, given as kinds of body, and a lecturing post. Nothing near the action shows who asked him to do what: no named bank, government or role, and no third-party proof. Social proof is absent.
findings.who_objects: A multilateral-bank staff member checking whether he has done this kind of work for bodies like theirs. Generic kinds of client are what every consultancy claims.

findings.where: Whole page: first screen, navigation and footer
findings.fault: The page never says where Mark is based. The margin notes give three cities but don't show his base country or the regions of his work.
findings.who_objects: A procurement officer, for whom region of experience and base country are part of the selection and the logistics. They have to go and look it up somewhere else.

findings.where: Top navigation (Profile, Articles and Presentations, Blog)
findings.fault: The navigation has no Contact entry, so a visitor who scrolled past the hero only finds the route to Mark at the bottom of the page.
findings.who_objects: A returning visitor who wants to get in touch from the top of the page and expects contact to be a standing part of the site, not a hero button.
